content:
It's another new week, and another streaming service is raising prices. ESPN announced this week that ESPN Select and ESPN Unlimited are both increasing their fees, with some Disney+ and Hulu bundle plans also seeing price hikes as a result.

The price increase was spotted by Sports Media Watch via ESPN's support page, with the new prices taking effect on September 17. Details as follows:

  • ESPN Select monthly: USD 14/month (was USD 13/month)
  • ESPN Select annual: USD 140/year (was USD 130/year)
  • ESPN Unlimited monthly: USD 32/month (was USD 30/month)
  • ESPN Unlimited annual: USD 320/year (was USD 300/year)

According to reports, this marks the first price increase from ESPN since it restructured its streaming strategy last year.

Meanwhile, some Disney-related bundle plans have also raised their prices in response to the ESPN streaming service hikes.

  • Disney+ (with ads), Hulu (with ads), and ESPN Select: USD 22/month (was USD 20/month)
  • Disney+ (no ads), Hulu (no ads), and ESPN Select: USD 33/month (was USD 30/month)

According to The Verge, the price increase also affects the legacy no-ads Hulu, Disney+, and ESPN Select bundle, which is no longer accepting new subscribers, with its monthly fee rising from USD 25 to USD 28.

The good news: ESPN Unlimited-related bundles are not affected by this price increase.

Peacock also announced a price hike last week, with monthly plans increasing by up to USD 3 and annual plans by up to USD 30. Apple has also recently raised prices for Apple Music and Apple One.
